records.text: At the Liberty Godparent Home in about 1994, residents were locked in their rooms, denied visitors, and photographed in ways the survivor considered strange.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #1 (Ep wcD2khO3rOA)

appearances.snippet: We were locked in our room. We weren't allowed visitors. ... They used to take weird pictures of us.

verification.notes: The recording establishes the survivor’s allegation, but no contemporaneous records or independent witness evidence were located to determine whether residents were locked in rooms, denied visitors, or photographed as described.

records.text: The survivor was moved alone to another room after a normal fetal check, and by the next morning staff said there was no heartbeat and induced labor.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #1 (Ep wcD2khO3rOA)

appearances.snippet: Everything was fine that night, and then they moved me, which was weird, they moved me to another room by myself. ... the next morning I all of a sudden didn't have a heartbeat and I had to go in. ... they had to induce the labor.

verification.notes: The survivor’s testimony is the only located source for the sequence of fetal monitoring, room transfer, loss of heartbeat, and induced labor.

records.text: Staff at the Liberty Godparent Home coerced residents to surrender babies for adoption because the program received adoption money.
records.speaker: Anonymous Source #1 (Ep wcD2khO3rOA)

appearances.snippet: they coerced us to give up the baby because they got money for adoption. It was some kind of adoption ring.

verification.notes: Independent reporting corroborates that multiple residents alleged coercive adoption pressure. The claim that the motive was adoption payments or that the program was an adoption ring was not established by the reviewed evidence.

records.text: After the survivor refused adoption, the home told her the fetus had no heartbeat, induced labor, did not let her see the baby, and sent her home without explaining burial arrangements.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: they induced labor after you said i don't want to give up my child... you never see your son... they tell your mom she's got to pick you up asap

verification.notes: This conclusion combines the survivor’s recollection with Owens’s inference. No medical, death, burial, or institutional records were available to establish the sequence or causal implication.

records.text: The Liberty Godparent Home was defending itself against allegations of coercion and manipulation, including pressure on residents to place children for adoption.
records.speaker: Rachel Branning

appearances.snippet: The Liberty Godparent Home... is defending itself against allegations of coercion and manipulation.

verification.notes: The statement is about the existence of reported allegations, not their adjudicated truth. VPM and the series publisher confirm allegations of pressure and coercion and the home’s public response.

sources.title: VPM: Liberty Lost coercion allegations
sources.relevance: Confirms that former residents alleged coercive pressure and that the home issued a response to WSET.

sources.title: Futuro Studios: Liberty Lost
sources.relevance: Describes the documented subject and claims of the reported series.

records.text: T. J. Raphael spent two years investigating the Liberty Godparent Home after connecting with former residents who were pregnant teenagers there in the 1990s and 2008.
records.speaker: T. J. Raphael

appearances.snippet: For the last two years, I've been investigating the maternity home after connecting with several residents who went through the home as pregnant teenage girls, both in the 1990s and in 2008.

verification.notes: Raphael’s on-record VPM interview and the published six-episode investigation confirm the multi-year reporting process and contact with former residents, including women connected to 2008 and earlier decades.

sources.title: VPM interview with T. J. Raphael
sources.relevance: Confirms Raphael began reporting after hearing from Abbi Johnson in 2022 and interviewed residents from the relevant periods.

records.text: Abbi Johnson felt abandoned when her parents sent her to the Liberty Godparent Home and said she did not meaningfully have a choice about placing her son for adoption.
records.speaker: Abbi Johnson

appearances.snippet: I really can't describe the sense of abandonment and fear and disassociation that you experience when your family abandons you... Did you ever really feel like you had a choice?... No

verification.notes: AP reporting independently quotes Johnson saying she wanted to parent and felt pressured into adoption; her feelings of abandonment are necessarily verified as attributed testimony rather than an objective institutional finding.

sources.title: AP/VPM: Abbi Johnson at Liberty Godparent Home
sources.relevance: Confirms Johnson was sent to the home, wanted to parent, and reported feeling pressured into adoption.

records.text: The Liberty Godparent Home said its staff and volunteers treated every person seeking assistance with compassion and integrity.
records.speaker: Liberty Godparent Home

appearances.snippet: They have treated every individual who has sought assistance. with compassion and integrity.

verification.notes: The public reporting confirms that the home issued the quoted defense. This verifies attribution of the statement, not that every resident was in fact treated with compassion and integrity.

sources.title: AP/VPM: Liberty Godparent Home response
sources.relevance: Reports the home’s statement that residents are educated on parenting and adoption and have freedom to choose.

sources.title: VPM: home issued WSET response
sources.relevance: Confirms the home issued a July 2025 statement to WSET.

records.text: Maternity-home residents should have received real support and options to parent their children, and the Liberty Godparent Home should not have shared ties with an adoption agency.
records.speaker: T. J. Raphael

appearances.snippet: These women should have been supported and provided with real options to keep and parent their children if that's what they wanted to do... But she says the godparent home shouldn't have ties to an adoption agency.

records.text: City records showed the Liberty Godparent Home and Family Life Services Adoption Agency shared an address, and Thomas Road Baptist Church founded the adoption agency.
records.speaker: Rachel Branning

appearances.snippet: According to city records, the godparent home and the family life services adoption agency share an address. Thomas Road Baptist Church founded family life services, according to their website.

verification.notes: Independent reporting confirms the home’s connection to an adjacent adoption agency and its Liberty/Falwell origins. The exact city-record wording and Thomas Road corporate history were not separately reproduced, so confidence is medium rather than high.
